stories.title: Stateless git server running directly on top of object storage
stories.social_post:
Hosting large Git repositories usually demands dedicated block storage, complex replication topologies, and persistent state on disk. Walgit challenges this model by operating as a stateless single binary placed directly in front of an object store like S3 or Google Cloud Storage.

The server has no leader election and maintains no internal database. Every compute instance functions purely as an ephemeral, disposable cache, treating the object store bucket as the canonical repository. It provides smart HTTP fetch and push, Git LFS support, fine-grained push policies, and an integrated browsing web interface.

Because the underlying storage engine offloads durability to cloud object storage, instances can scale horizontally or restart without data loss or re-synchronization overhead. Repositories can grow far larger than the local disk of any individual worker node.

Decoupling compute from storage transforms operational maintenance for version control infrastructure into a truly stateless problem.
stories.why_read: Learn how Walgit implements a stateless Git server backed directly by object storage rather than local disks. It illustrates a clean architectural pattern for scaling repository hosting without databases or coordination.

stories.title: Tolerating complete cloud outages using an independent stand-in platform
stories.social_post:
True cross-cloud resilience requires complete isolation rather than shared abstractions across cloud providers. Monzo built a secondary banking platform on Google Cloud Platform that operates as an independent stand-in to their primary AWS infrastructure.

Instead of trying to keep complex distributed databases synchronously locked across two clouds, the stand-in platform uses unique services tailored specifically to core survival features. Customers can still withdraw cash, make card payments, and execute bank transfers even during a catastrophic primary cloud failure.

Each platform maintains its own database, queueing mechanisms, and distributed locks, allowing both sides to make independent transactional decisions. By avoiding synchronized distributed state during normal operations, Monzo prevents cascading failures from infecting the backup environment.

The most dependable disaster recovery system is not a seamless mirror, but a radically decoupled life raft.
stories.why_read: Learn how Monzo built an isolated secondary platform across different cloud providers to guarantee high availability for critical banking functions during catastrophic outages.

stories.title: Rootless daemonless containers isolate agent tool calls and code
stories.social_post:
Running untrusted code from language model tool calls inside full-fat container engines introduces needless operational complexity and memory bloat. Traditional runtimes like Docker depend on long-running background daemons, socket communication, and heavy resource allocations that slow down fast, isolated execution loops.

Kern provides a minimalist alternative by packaging a rootless, kernel-enforced container sandbox into a single 1.5 megabyte static binary without any background daemon. It boots in a few milliseconds and consumes zero memory when idle, using native Linux kernel primitives to isolate code execution directly.

For engineers integrating Model Context Protocol servers into developer workflows, this architecture removes the friction of managing persistent container state. You get process isolation for agent tool invocations through a lightweight toolchain that drops straight into Cursor, Claude Code, or command-line pipelines.

Sandboxing autonomous agents should not require running a massive container orchestration stack on every developer workstation.
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how a daemonless, single-binary container runtime isolates LLM tool executions with zero idle memory overhead.

stories.title: S3 compatibility does not ensure write-ahead log performance
stories.social_post:
Building a write-ahead log directly on top of object storage sounds like an architectural dream. By leveraging compare-and-swap operations through ETag conditional writes, systems can achieve durable, leaderless logs without maintaining dedicated consensus nodes or raw disks.

However, API compatibility does not guarantee viable write latency. A write-ahead log presents a pathological access pattern for cloud object stores because it relies entirely on small, tightly serialized conditional writes. While AWS S3, S3 Express One Zone, Tigris, and Cloudflare R2 all satisfy correctness guarantees and avoid orphaned writes, their latency characteristics diverge drastically under contention.

Standard S3 tiers incur round-trip and commit overhead that can stall high-throughput commit pipelines. In contrast, low-latency tiers such as S3 Express One Zone dramatically shrink the commit tail, though at a significantly higher cost profile.

Before adopting cloud object stores as the primary WAL for your distributed storage engine, profile your serialization latency under realistic payload sizes. Correctness over the wire does not automatically deliver production throughput.
stories.why_read: Read this to understand why S3 compatibility fails to predict write-ahead log performance across object storage providers. You will learn how serialized conditional writes reveal massive latency variations across major platforms.

stories.title: Explicit state machines make long running agent workflows reliable
stories.social_post:
Long-running AI agents fail most frequently because procedural state is stuffed entirely into conversational context. As token history grows, the original goal fades, verification steps get bypassed, and failures turn into endless unrecoverable loops.

StateM addresses this architectural defect by pulling workflow orchestration out of model memory and into an external, versioned state machine. The agent operates across explicit stages for planning, execution, verification, and repair, where every transition requires programmatic proof before execution advances.

On Terminal-Bench benchmarks, enforcing deterministic state transitions and external runbooks lifted descriptive accuracy to nearly eighty-nine percent on long-horizon tasks. Moving state tracking to disk and deterministic code keeps the prompt focused solely on the immediate step, preserving attention and slashing context pollution.

Reliable autonomous agents require deterministic state boundaries instead of hoping a model remembers its own plan.
stories.why_read: Read this to understand why long AI agent runs degrade when procedural state lives only in conversation history. You will learn how offloading agent execution into an inspectable state machine enables verifiable transitions and recovery.

stories.title: Boosting uncensored Qwen3.8 inference to 125 tokens per second
stories.social_post:
Running local models for agent loops usually stalls on token generation speed rather than raw compute. A recent benchmark showed that tuning vLLM on a single ninety-six gigabyte GPU can push a twenty-seven billion parameter model from forty-four tokens per second up to one hundred and twenty-five tokens per second.

The primary bottleneck in agent loops is not model parameter count, but memory bandwidth and KV cache growth during multi-turn tool execution. Moving from BF16 to FP8 precision halved memory pressure, while layering multi-token prediction and speculative decoding via DFlash2 delivered an immediate seventy-two percent speedup.

Keeping the context window around two hundred and fourteen thousand tokens allowed the entire working set and KV cache to fit comfortably without spilling over into system RAM.

Optimizing local inference for agentic workloads comes down to context management and precision tuning rather than simply buying larger clusters.
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how combining FP8 quantization and speculative decoding drastically accelerates LLM inference speeds on high-VRAM hardware. It offers practical benchmarking data and architectural insights for running long-context models cost-effectively.

stories.title: Building a tiny language model from scratch removes the magic
stories.social_post:
Most engineers interact with large language models through high-level APIs or monolithic libraries, treating everything beneath the HTTP request as a black box. Understanding how token prediction transforms into autonomous agent behavior requires building each layer by hand.

The From Gradients to ChatGPT project structures this path like the classic Nand to Tetris curriculum. Starting from scalar automatic differentiation, it moves progressively through tensor operations, tokenizers, multi-head attention, and transformer training before tackling supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, retrieval-augmented generation, and tool-calling agent loops.

The entire curriculum operates under a strict constraint: every model and pipeline must run locally on an Apple silicon laptop without remote GPUs or external cloud compute. By training a miniature transformer with a few million parameters on a local corpus, engineers observe how gradients, loss curves, and sampling strategies behave in practice without astronomical compute costs.

Demystifying modern machine learning infrastructure starts when you replace opaque library calls with your own tensor math and agent execution loops.
stories.why_read: Read this to understand how modern language models operate from first principles by building every layer locally from scratch. You will develop a durable mental model of the entire stack, from basic autodiff to a functional chat assistant.
